# ethereum-optimism/specs Monthly Report (June 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
June 2026 was characterized by the formalization of the Karst Osaka and Interop protocol specifications, signaling a transition from experimental drafts to stable protocol candidates. Significant engineering effort was directed toward resolving critical synchronization deadlocks between `op-node` and `op-reth`, alongside the introduction of new transaction types and metering schemas. The month also saw a focus on "Safer Safes" and robust recovery runbooks, ensuring that as the Superchain scales, its security and operational resilience keep pace with technical complexity.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol & Hardfork Specifications
The project made substantial progress in defining the next evolution of the OP Stack, specifically focusing on the Osaka upgrade and Interoperability.
*   **Karst Osaka:** Documentation for Karst Osaka changes was integrated, providing a comprehensive overview of the protocol updates ([#904](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/904)).
*   **Post-Execution & SDM:** New specifications were established for the `0x7D` Post-Execution Transaction envelope and version-1 Sequencer-Defined Metering (SDM). These updates include new payload schemas and glossary definitions essential for advanced sequencer rebate logic ([#908](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/908)).
*   **Interop Reclassification:** A strategic move was initiated to reclassify Interop specifications from "experimental" to "lagoon," aligning its activation with features like SDM ([#915](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/915)).

### Security and Smart Contracts
*   **Safer Safes:** A high-level specification for "Safer Safes" contracts was introduced. This work defines critical invariants for liveness recovery, transaction timelocks, and module-scope properties to enhance the security of multisig operations within the ecosystem ([#914](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/914)).

### Tooling and Testing Infrastructure
*   **op-reth-test-engine:** Development began on a minimal in-test Execution Layer (EL) for `op-e2e/actions`. This approach leverages the actual `op-reth` stack for storage and validation, aiming for Rust action-test parity without reimplementing core logic ([#20415](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20415)).
*   **CI Optimization:** The team addressed flaky e2e fuzz tests by implementing lazy generation for alloc types, significantly reducing binary startup times and preventing CircleCI timeouts ([#21191](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21191)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Sync & Stability:** Several issues regarding sequencer sync stability and `op-supernode` integration were resolved. Notably, a configuration error in the devstack interop preset—where the EL was incorrectly shared between nodes—was fixed ([#21158](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21158)).
*   **Interop Failsafe:** The issue where the `op-reth` transaction pool failed to resume after a failsafe event was resolved by identifying that `op-rbuilder` also required a restart to clear evicted state ([#21149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21149)).
*   **Osaka Drafts:** The long-standing draft specifications for Osaka on L2 were officially finalized and closed ([#903](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/903)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Reth Engine Deadlocks:** A critical active investigation involves a cyclic deadlock in `op-reth`'s `StateTrieOverlayManager`. This issue causes CL sync recovery to stall and appears linked to locks held across `rayon` compute tasks. Patches are currently undergoing soak testing ([#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21076)).
*   **Recovery Runbooks:** Following the decision not to implement automatic recovery for interop reorgs in `op-conductor` ([#20006](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20006)), a new effort is underway to create manual recovery runbooks for handling invalid interop messages ([#21161](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21161)).
*   **SDM Rebate Limits:** Ongoing discussion regarding protocol-level upper bounds for sequencer rebates to prevent potential DoS vectors via `MAX_GAS_LIMIT` ([#20709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20709)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month's activity highlights a deep technical collaboration between the Optimism specs maintainers and the `reth` development team (Paradigm), particularly in diagnosing low-level engine API deadlocks. There is also a clear shift toward operational maturity, evidenced by the move from automated "experimental" fixes to the development of structured runbooks and manual intervention strategies for complex interop scenarios. Discussions around `op-revm` support indicate a commitment to staying synchronized with the broader Ethereum upstream (e.g., the Amsterdam hardfork support in REVM v111).
